Definition of Sequences
Introduction – Test Automation Framework o The term "Test Automation" refers to the process of reviewing and validating
slides.body:
o The term "Test Automation" refers to the process of reviewing and validating a
software carried out in a totally automatic manner, exempting the tester from
manual interventions.
This strategy allows a substantial reduction in the time required for testing and
re-testing activities.
Test Automation also allows you to dispose of the bugtracking phase thanks to
the process output, called a report, in which not only the result of the test is
highlighted but above all, in case of failure, the cause for which the validation
has given a negative result.
In order to carry out tests automatically, it is necessary to define a UUT (Unit
Under Test), in our case the control unit, and a coded structure that allows
automatic interaction with the UUT, defined as a Framework, which also
includes the definition of the VeriStand project on which we are working.

slides.title: o As you can see in the previous slide, the interface contains several sections: sector '1' contains code syntax The ref
slides.body:
The reference "2" is in the "Primitives" section which contains (a) the folder of the
various types of "Variables" possible to be declared, (b) the folder of "Expressions" or
assignments, through which to assign values to parameters/variables or references,
(c) the folder of the structures that contains the loops that can be used (while, do
while, for cycles...), the conditionals (if/else) or the "Multitasking" in case a
simultaneous management of several instructions is required (Management of
multiple tasks such as executing several instructions at the same time, stopping one
before the others, and so on), (d) the "Advanced" folder that allows you to invoke a
state for suspending the sequence in real time while the primary control loop iterates
in real time, (e) the "Miscellaneous" folder that allows you to document the code or
create a list of states
It is the panel of the quantities involved/recalled in the sequence, in particular: (a) The
"Return Variable", i.e. the output indicator of the sequence, which can be a Boolean
(in case you check whether the test is OK or KO) or a double (real numerical value),
(b) the "Parameters", ie the input variables of the sequence / function, (c) The "Local
Variables", from the name local variables defined within the sequence, (d) the
"Channel References", i.e. a link to the parameters defined internally by the project
(Aliases, CAN signals, software variables, analog and/or digital signals)
The "References" section contains a list of all the real-time sequences referred to in
the selected real sequence
Finally, the Panel that indicates errors or warnings following compilation

slides.title: VF Automation
Stimulus Profile Automation
o The priority operation is the recall of the "VeriStand Project", through the path of the folder on the left "VeriStand
slides.body:
folder on the left "VeriStand Control", thus being able to open or close the project and
actively control it.
We then move on to the recall of the various Real-Time Sequences, which represent
the individual test cases of the VF, through the command "Real-Time Sequence Call"
and in which, as observed in the previous slide, it is necessary to define the "File
Path" of the sequence, the "Target Name", or the identification of the target with all its
specifications, such as "the Operating System", "IP Address ( address)", the tasks of
the processor, the "Data Processing Loop" and other settings such as the processor
execution mode (Low Latency or Parallel), the frequency rate of the DAQ and the
DIOs, the "warmup time" and finally, perhaps the most significant, the "Target rate
(Hz)" and the "Timing Source Timeout (ms)".
Finally, the evaluation of the Pass/Fail is defined which, as in the case of the single
Real-Time Sequence, can consist of "Boolean", "Always Pass" or a
"NumericBoundsCheck" output in the case of control against a predefined threshold.
Finally, the "Update Parameters" function that allows you to modify the input
parameters to study the reaction of the UUT to the test.
Once the writing is complete, we proceed to the compilation and the subsequent
launch.
At the end of the "Run", a sort of Report will be generated that simply indicates the
result of each Real-Time Sequence.
